pins.title: Plan the canyon
pins.sub: Veterans Day is a fee-free day: check nps.gov for who qualifies. The South Rim is open all year. Rim trails can be icy, and the climb out takes about twice as long as the walk down.

pins.kicker: Beanie too hot on the climb?
pins.title: Cover the ears
items: Bare ears go numb fast in the wind
A fleece headband covers ears and forehead
The top of your head stays open to vent
Fits under a cap or a jacket hood
Packs flat into a pocket

pins.title: Wear a balaclava
pins.sub: Hood, face panel and long neck in one fleece piece. Pull it over your nose in the wind, push it under your chin when you warm up.

pins.title: Flip it
pins.sub: Water freezes from the top, so carry the bottle upside down and the lid stays clear. A neoprene sleeve on a strap slows the cold and keeps the water at your hip.

pins.kicker: Cold feet in your sleeping bag?
pins.title: Dry socks on
pins.sub: The socks you hiked in are damp with sweat. Change into a clean, dry pair before bed and eat a small snack. Ours are 80% merino, cushioned crew, sold as 1 pair.

pins.title: Slow down
items: Expect ice in shade and on north slopes
Put traction on before the ice
Short steps, weight over your feet
Poles help you balance
Too steep or icy? Turn back
pins.sub: Free guide on the blog: tap the pin.

pins.title: Don't forget
items: A warm hat and gloves
A spare pair of dry socks
A headlamp: it gets dark early
A hot drink or warm water
Snacks you can eat with gloves on
pins.sub: Free printable checklist: tap the pin.

pins.title: Book early
pins.sub: Going-to-the-Sun Road often opens fully only in late June or July. A printable trip planner with the season, entry rules, lodging and day hikes.

pins.title: Stay back
pins.sub: Ice can break off without warning. A printable hiking safety guide: weather, cold, heat and getting lost, plus an emergency reference card.
